facts.title: A Supermoon Can Look 14% Bigger and 30% Brighter Than the Faintest Full Moon
facts.summary: The Moon's orbit is not a perfect circle, so its distance from Earth keeps changing.

facts.title: Alan Shepard Smuggled a Golf Club to the Moon and Hit Two Balls
facts.summary: On February 6, 1971, during the Apollo 14 mission, astronaut Alan Shepard became the first person to play golf on another world.

facts.title: Apollo Astronauts Brought 382 Kilograms of the Moon Back to Earth
facts.summary: Apollo astronauts collected 382 kilograms of lunar rock and soil from six places on the Moon's surface.

facts.title: Apollo Astronauts Said Moon Dust Smelled Like Spent Gunpowder
facts.summary: The Moon has a smell, but only astronauts have ever caught it.

facts.title: China's Chang'e-4 Made the First Ever Landing on the Moon's Far Side
facts.summary: No spacecraft had ever landed on the far side of the Moon until January 3, 2019.

facts.title: During a Total Lunar Eclipse, the Moon Glows With Earth's Sunsets
facts.summary: In a total lunar eclipse the Moon slips completely into Earth's darkest shadow, yet it does not disappear.

facts.title: India Became the First Country to Land Near the Moon's South Pole
facts.summary: On August 23, 2023, India's Chandrayaan-3 mission set its Vikram lander down near the Moon's south pole, at roughly 70 degrees south latitude.

facts.title: Lumpy Lunar Gravity Brought Down an Apollo 16 Satellite in Just 35 Days
facts.summary: The Moon's gravity is not smooth.

facts.title: NASA Crashed a Rocket Into the Moon in 2009 to Hunt for Water
facts.summary: In the early morning of October 9, 2009, NASA deliberately smashed a spent Centaur rocket stage into Cabeus crater near the Moon's south pole.

facts.title: Nobody Saw the Moon's Far Side Until a Soviet Probe Photographed It in 1959
facts.summary: For all of human history, the far side of the Moon was hidden from view.

facts.title: Shadowed Craters at the Moon's South Pole Are Colder Than Pluto
facts.summary: Some of the coldest temperatures ever measured in the solar system were found on the Moon.

facts.title: Thanks to a Gentle Wobble, We Can See About 59% of the Moon From Earth
facts.summary: The Moon always keeps the same face toward Earth because it rotates exactly once for every orbit; in a sense, its day and its year are the same length.

facts.title: The Moon Drifts About 3.8 Centimeters Farther From Earth Every Year
facts.summary: The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth.

facts.title: The Moon Is Shrinking, and Apollo Seismometers Caught It Quaking
facts.summary: The Moon is still geologically restless.

facts.title: The Moon Was Probably Born When a Mars-Sized World Hit the Young Earth
facts.summary: Most scientists think the Moon formed from wreckage.

facts.title: The Moon's Largest Crater Is About 2,500 Kilometers Wide
facts.summary: The biggest scar on the Moon is the South Pole-Aitken basin, a giant impact crater roughly 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) across.

facts.title: Tree Seeds Orbited the Moon on Apollo 14 and Grew Into Moon Trees
facts.summary: Some trees growing in the United States have been to the Moon.
